- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after sharp spikes.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) and price is trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect bearish sentiment’s fading or reversal.
- After a strong upward spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overcorrects downward — cap downward revisions to avoid excessive lag.
- When sentiment flips from negative to positive (or vice versa), model lags 1–2 days in adjusting; apply a 1-day lag correction to align with sentiment shift.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon — if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misaligns with cycle phase — match forecast to sentiment’s dominant recent trend, not just average.
